evidence.quoted_text:
"manager_restarted": (
            (((manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager") or {})
             .get("pid") or 0) > 0
            and (((manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                 .get("pid") or 0) > 0
            and (manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("pid")
            != (manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("pid")
            and bool(((manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                     .get("invocation_id"))
            and bool(((manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                     .get("invocation_id"))
            and (manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("invocation_id")
            != (manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("invocation_id")),
evidence.reason: The current `manager_restarted` check only requires positive, differing manager PIDs and nonempty, differing invocation IDs across the manager before/after snapshots. It does not require those snapshots to come from the same guest boot. A guest reboot changes both the manager PID and invocation ID, so it can satisfy `manager_restarted`; the later separate reboot check can still pass because `boot_id_changed` compares its own before/after reboot boot IDs. This is a false-positive path in the feasibility evidence, and binding the manager-restart check to a nonempty equal guest boot ID is a routine correctness fix.
